To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a lower viscosity threshold for the start of injection can be defined by the rheometer and thereby leakage can be decreased; (2) an injection break can be used to address leakages; (3) the viscosity of the cement decreases with time; (4) the hardening rate is increased by body temperature; (5) the viscosity of different cements can be measured by the rheometer.

the direct measurement of cement viscosity during vertebraoplasty can be used to define a lower viscosity threshold for the start of the injection, which can be used to decrease the risk of cement leakage and that the acceleration in cement hardening at body temperature can minimize the risk for cement leakages by addressing these with a short injection pause.
the viscosity of PMMA-based cement during vertebroplaty can be assessed with the developed device and that this can help clinicians to minimize the risk of cement leakage.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the clinical investigation of PMMA cement viscosity during verteproplasty as well as the in vitro characterization of the cement hardening process.
a better understanding of cement viscosity in relation to vertebroplasy and its complications, and to provide a tool to improve patient safety.
a clinical and in vitro study of the viscosity of polymethylmethacylate (PMMA)-based cements during percutaneous injection procedures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a viscosity of 10-15 Pa·s should be used for the start of the injection procedure, and the injection should be interrupted when the viscosity reaches 100 Pa·s.
the viscosity of PMMA-based cement is an important factor in the occurrence of leakage during vertebrooplasty.
the cement viscosity should be measured during vertebrooplasty in order to avoid leakage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cement viscosity during vertroplasty is highly dependent on the injection device and the ambient temperature.
viscosity measurements can help to improve the safety of vertebroplasties.
the rheometer is a useful tool in the context of vertebroplasties and that the cement viscosity should be measured during the procedure to avoid leakage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
viscosity measurements in vivo and in vitro are of great importance to improve vertebroplastic procedures.
a rheometer system is a valuable instrument in the context of vertebroplasties to assess the cement viscosity and to make adjustments to the injection procedure.

the viscosity of the PMMA-based cemets used in vertebroplasties can be measured in real time during the operation and that the cement hardens significantly faster when the body temperature is reached.
